The booking/event data (destinationCalendar, references, organizer, etc.) pertains to the booking owner/organizer, yet the code does not use the organizer’s credentials (even though `booking.user` is fetched with `credentials: true` and then unused). This is a concrete correctness/security concern: calendar updates may fail for attendees (no integrations) or run under the wrong account when the caller has integrations, rather than under the organizer/booking-owner context.

apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:44 — raw tRPC error code and untranslated server message are surfaced in the toast (fallback on line 45 is dead because the template string is always truthy), leaking internal error codes/messages to the UI (`const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;`; confidence 50; severity P3)

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` the `onError` handler builds `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` and then calls `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")`. A template string is always truthy, even when `err.data?.code` is undefined (it becomes the literal "undefined") and `t(err.message)` may be an untranslated/raw server message key/value. Therefore the fallback `unable_to_add_guests` toast is effectively dead, and the UI will display internal tRPC error codes and potentially untranslated server messages.
